thread:
Kevin (customer): Hi team — getting failures when calling our registered tool via the API after today's rename. Error: `tool_not_found` and returns 404. Repro steps below.
Maya (Support): sorry to hear that, Kevin. Can you paste the request body you used and the value in `function_call.name`?
Kevin (customer): sure — minimal payload:
```json
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-alpha-1\",
  \"input\": \"run report\",
  \"function_call\": { \"name\": \"GenerateReport\", \"arguments\": \"{\\\"period\\\":\\\"Q4\\\"}\" }
}
```
Maya (Support): thanks — two quick questions: did the tool get renamed in your registry (e.g., `GenerateReport` -> `generate_report`) or were aliases added? Also which API region / account id?
Kevin (customer): we renamed to `generate_report` (lowercase) as part of a refactor. We added an alias but not sure if it propagated. Using hosted region us-west-2 under acct `acct-42`.
Maya (Support): OK. I'm kicking this to eng to check registry sync and whether aliases are case-sensitive. @James can you take a look? /cc @Ravi (registry)
James (Eng): looking. Can you include the full response body and any X-Request-Id from the failing call?
Kevin (customer): full response:
```json
{
  \"error\": {
    \"code\": \"tool_not_found\",
    \"message\": \"Tool '\\\"GenerateReport\\\"' not found.\"
  },
  \"request_id\": \"r-8a7f3d2c\"
}
```
DeployBot: registry-sync-job started for acct-42 (job id: rs-20260311-9) :gear:
James (Eng): I pulled the trace for r-8a7f3d2c — the router forwarded to tool-resolver which queried the registry with key `GenerateReport`. The DB lookup is case-sensitive because the service uses the primary `tool_name` index (collation=binary). It returned no rows.
Ravi (Registry): yeah — looks like the alias creation step for the rename failed in the background job due to a partial index race during the midnight migration window. Alias record `generate_report`->`tool_id:tr-123` exists, but `GenerateReport` alias wasn't created (we had an older uppercase-matching cleanup that removed duplicates).
Priya (Oncall): severity? Customer is blocked from automated runs. Recommend hotfix + customer workaround.
Maya (Support): Kevin, temporary workaround: set `function_call.name` to the new exact name `generate_report` (all lowercase) or use the explicit `tool_id` in the call if your client supports it. Will that work for you?
Kevin (customer): yes switching to `generate_report` works, but we have many clients who still call `GenerateReport` from older code. Can you advise on fix timeline?
James (Eng): plan: 1) create a small backfill that inserts missing alias rows for case variants of the same tool_id, 2) deploy a migration to make lookups case-insensitive at resolver layer (use lowercased index) as a follow-up. Backfill estimate: ~2 hours, then quick deploy of resolver fix can be done in ~4 hours after testing.
Ravi (Registry): I'm running the backfill now against acct-42 first to validate. I'll post logs here.
Ravi (Registry): backfill log sample: `2026-03-11T14:22:03Z INFO backfill created alias GenerateReport -> tr-123 for acct-42`
DeployBot: backfill task rs-20260311-9 completed for acct-42 :white_check_mark:
James (Eng): validated with an emulated request — `GenerateReport` now resolves to tr-123. Kevin can you retry?
Kevin (customer): retried — success! Response is 200 and tool executed. Thanks. :tada:
Maya (Support): marking this as resolved for the immediate issue. We'll keep the resolver migration on the roadmap to avoid recurrence.
Anna (PM): adding post-incident item: improve rename docs and add registry sync monitoring + alert.
Maya (Support): follow-up action items: 1) confirm backfill for other affected accounts (Ravi) 2) schedule resolver change + test plan (James) 3) update docs and dev-notes on aliasing behavior (Anna).
Ravi (Registry): will run backfill across impacted accounts overnight and post a list in #eng-ml.
Kevin (customer): appreciate the quick turnaround. Do you provide any postmortem?
Maya (Support): yes — we'll share a short incident summary and actions once the resolver migration is scheduled. Thanks for reporting, Kevin.
James (Eng): one more note — temporary workaround for other customers: set header `X-Tool-Name-CaseInsensitive: true` to force lowercasing at the edge for now (we're enabling it per-customer as needed).
Kevin (customer): OK we'll roll that out while you deploy the permanent fix.
Maya (Support): closing thread — reopen if anything else pops up. :slightly_smiling_face:
